GROK
Updated 2026-09-06
Sources: your Grok bookmark folder (1196 posts)

NEW TODAY
- Folder now 1196 posts (4 new since Sep 5)
- Testers (testerlabor, Mr_Salio, ElonEconomyX): Grok 4.7 Beta Sat Sep 12 / next week - 2.1T (+600B vs 4.6); frames possible beat of GPT-6 Astra at ~10x cheaper; SpaceX supplemental data; better reasoning/coding/agents; initial training done
- Testers (joehansen): El Salvador Grok tutoring - Dec 2025 deal aimed at 1M+ students / 5k+ schools; 171-school OECD PISA for Schools pilot (Jun 2026) above national avg / near Germany-range peers; World Bank: pilot not whole system; >1k schools built; nationwide ~18 months

WHAT IT IS
- Grok is xAI / SpaceXAI's assistant: chat, voice, Imagine, Build, and the model API, in the Grok app, https://t.co/UvO8aC6o4n, and on X.
- This folder is Grok-the-product (app, models, voice, Imagine-in-Grok, plans). Separate folders exist for Grok Bot, Grok Build, and Grok Imagine.
- Grok Bot (persistent agents on a shared computer) and Grok Build (coding harness / Build mode) show up here when they ship inside SuperGrok or the Grok app.

GROK 4.6 / MODELS
- Grok 4.6 launched 2026-08-12. Elon: smart, fast, amazing bang for buck. Also #1 on Databricks.
- Same 1.5T base as 4.5; testers credit a big SFT + RL jump. Stronger multi-step reasoning, coding, agents, frontend taste.
- API: $2 input / $6 output per million tokens. Live in the Grok app, API, Cursor, OpenClaw, Hermes Agent. Testers: also on Perplexity and Perplexity Computer.
- Reported leads: GDPVal-AA v2, AA-Briefcase, Harvey LAB; #1 CursorBench 3.2 (Extra High 70.8% at ~$2.81/task vs Fable 5 Max 70.5% at ~$17.32); #1 VISTA; #1 MedAgentBench; testers (joehansen, XFreeze): GPQA Diamond — 4.6 high led ~95%, then #2 at 94.9% after Gemini 3.8 Flash high took #1 at 95.3% (Sep 2). Testers: 4.6 High tied Opus 5 Max at 59 on the AA Agentic Index. Artificial Analysis ~61 — testers (XFreeze, cb_doge, Sep 4): ties newly released GPT-6 Astra at 61; beats Astra Max on Agentic Index 59 vs 51, τ³-Banking 51% vs 41%, non-hallucination 66% vs 49%, GDPval-AA v2 1,730 vs 1,629. Still matches GPT-5.6 Sol at up to 5x lower API price.
- Testers (XEthanai): WANDR puts 4.6 on the Pareto frontier vs Fable 5 at >60% less cost. Standard-mode latency ~912 min per complex prompt; keep Fast and Extra High disabled to protect monthly limits. Non-enterprise testers say Cursor or Grok Build can be better value than the standalone API.
- Nvidia: trained and served on GB300 NVL72. SpaceXAI is writing its own C/C++ inference stacked on that silicon (XFreeze).
- Elon: 4.7 initial training done, expected to exceed current models. Testers (JayaNayak21, RoundtableSpace, astropol0, testerlabor, mark_k, tetsuoai, joehansen): ~Sep 12 / "10 days"; 2.1T (+600B vs 4.6); first real architecture/scale step (1.5T → 2.1T); coding + writing upgrades; SpaceX engineering data pass; Elon says good chance of surpassing every current model. Testers (astropol0): framed as possible Fable 5level frontier. Testers (Mr_Salio / joehansen / XFreeze Sep 4): SpaceX supplemental training (rockets, Raptor, Starship, Starlink, manufacturing, orbital systems) — framed as inheriting SpaceX engineering DNA; larger 2.1T stack expected better + more token-efficient; days away. Testers (joehansen): 4.6 stays 1.5T; AA ~61 with Sol; API $2/$6 vs Sol $5/$30.
- Testers (mark_k, tetsuoai): Grok 4.7 ~September 12 based on Elon's "10 days" timeline; expected 2.1T with improved coding and writing (anticipation).
- Testers (testerlabor, MarioNawfal Sep 5): Grok 4.7 coming next week / around the corner - 2.1T (+40% / +600B vs 4.6); SpaceX engineering data; persistent Grok Bot cloud teams; Elon: will exceed all current models.
- Testers (testerlabor, Mr_Salio, ElonEconomyX Sep 6): Grok 4.7 Beta Sat Sep 12 / next week first look; 2.1T (+600B vs 4.6); frames possible beat of GPT-6 Astra at ~10x cheaper; SpaceX supplemental data; better reasoning/coding/agents; initial training done.
- Testers (bridgebench): frames 4.6 as the turning point for real workflows; claims fastest / cheapest flagship on BridgeBench (~0.1 behind GPT 5.6 Sol); expects 4.7 (2.1T) to be a frontier coding model (opinion).
- Testers (joehansen): on an agent-task board (Gmail/Sheets/Slack/Salesforce/Zendesk/Jira/HubSpot), Grok 4.5 high ~80% objectives (~$0.38/task) vs Gemini 3.7 Flash high ~80% (~$0.19); notes 4.6 is not on that board.
- Testers (Thisiskeena, XFreeze, joehansen, teslaownersSV): LatchBio biosecurity benchmark — Grok 4.6 only model above 50% on both refusing disguised bio threats (59.2%) and completing legitimate research (64.8%); avg 62.1% across harnesses (MiniSWE 64.2%, Pi 63.0%, Grok Build 59.0%); pathogen surveillance 53.5% (ahead of GPT-5.6 Sol); intent/reasoning over blanket filters; near frontier on therapeutics / variant / epigenomics / spatial / single-cell.
- Bookmark testers: Grok 5.0 is the AGI-scale bet, still training on Colossus II (~220k GPUs). Testers (joehansen, testerlabor Sep 3): still training on ~6T & ~10T at Colossus 2 (world's largest AI supercluster framing); several times the 4.7 stack; expected end of year.
- Usage resets: grab a reset token in Grok settings. Testers: weekly resets do not stack; use them before the next one lands.
- Testers (LaceyPresley): SuperGrok Heavy credits can burn mid-week (reset Saturday)  compute/power rationing, not model capability, is the felt bottleneck.
- Lineage testers cite: Grok 1 → 1.5 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 4.1 → 4.2 → 4.3 → 4.5 → 4.6.

- Paste a video link; Grok watches, summarizes, and answers without an upload (cb_doge).

- CAD: official grok nudge to use 4.6 for CAD.

IMAGINE / IMAGE VIDEO

- Launch-week limits were reset once via a settings token. Heavy has high but finite caps; app / Bot / Cursor caps do not share one bucket.
- Testers (XEthanai): keep Fast and Extra High modes disabled to protect monthly limits.
- Promo stacking is unofficial. Testers expect xAI to close the $99 Heavy hole.
- Grok is the product testers call "based" / truth-seeking; that is opinion, not a safety spec. Official (elonmusk): Grok providing schooling in El Salvador. Testers (joehansen Sep 6): Dec 2025 curriculum-aligned tutor aimed at 1M+ students across 5k+ public schools; 171-school OECD PISA for Schools pilot (Jun 2026) above national average and in range of high-income European peers (Germany); World Bank: pilot scores not whole system yet; build past 1k schools; plan to cover all public schools in ~18 months. Testers (XFreeze): frames Grok as the most neutral / truth-seeking major AI and argues it belongs in education — teach kids how to think, not ideology (opinion).
- Testers (LatchBio writeups via Thisiskeena / XFreeze / joehansen / teslaownersSV): 4.6 balances biosecurity refusal with useful dual-use science (see GROK 4.6 / MODELS).

USEFUL WORKFLOWS
- Phone: Action Button → Grok; swipe to Build for a one-line mini-app; swipe to Imagine for a clip; Voice + screen share for live help.
- Daily brief: Voice connector → podcast or memo of the day (grok, Aug 10).
- Inbox: automation on matching email (XFreeze).
- Video: paste a link, ask for a summary or Q&A.
- Coding / CAD / frontend: 4.6 in the Grok app, Cursor, or API. Testers like it for games, HTML simulations, laser/ILDA, and CAD.
- Research / real jobs: 4.6 on GDPval-style work (doctors, lawyers, accountants) at $2/$6.

Some thoughts on whether Astra is AGI.

AGI is hard to define - but I particularly like @fchollet's definition - that we'll have AGI when "the exercise of creating tasks that are easy for regular humans but hard for AI becomes simply impossible." By this standard, across the board, Astra is not AGI - it (likely) cannot perform long-horizon embodied tasks (making a cup of coffee, assembling a piece of IKEA furniture), could not play real-time multiplayer games like CS:GO or Overwatch, and lacks audio input (which makes it obviously subhuman at a wide variety of audio tasks - even stuff as simple as transcribing words from audio w/out whisper)!

However, I think this is slightly unfair to Astra - it exists in a world of much more limited I/O than humans do - it takes text and images as input, and can output text - some of which is tool-calls. And in this regime, I think a case can be made for Astra being AGI-like - i.e. its very hard to find a task that can be done on a computer, the inputs to which are text and images, and the desired outputs of which are text and images, where Astra is *worse* than the average human who is familiar with computer use.

A prominent example of this is of course ARC-AGI-3, which Astra essentially saturates (fewer actions than the median human on 96% of levels). It crushes the human baselines on ARC-AGI-1 (98.5% vs 64.2%) and 2 (95.0% vs 60%). 

Astra is also superhuman (as in better than a median human in America/the world) on any form of STEM/classicailly verifiable knowledge task one can think of - the benchmarks its evaluated on typically show it massing or surpassing human *expert* performance. I'd be highly surprised if one could find a broad, non-gotcha task that showed otherwise. Some evidence that leads me to believe this below:

GPQA - Astra gets 96%. PHD Expert gets 69.7% (81.3% among original validators).

BrowseComp - Astra gets 91.5%. 29.2% was the average human baseline.

HealthBench Professional - Astra gets 63.4 points, versus 43.7 points for human experts with internet access and no time limit.

Most other benchmarks share this pattern, afaik.

This isn't to say for a domain-specific task STEM/verifiable knowledge task, there exists no human that surpasses Astra - I'm sure there are many - but the average human surpassing Astra? Likely not. 

Furthermore, Astra appears to be a generational leap in computer use - it can get diamonds in Minecraft  (https://t.co/Fhcg8dqfPl), and beat Portal (https://t.co/n5iJfklXh1). For the latter, the game pauses while Astra thinks - so its not entirely human-matched - but this is inevitable, given the way Astra is bound to the world is through a strict inspect image -> call tool -> inspect image loop (one that it is trained to use quite well!), instead of the more continuous interaction humans have between sensory input, motor control, and higher-level thought.  Similarly, it can also use Blender (https://t.co/kefnfR6LEe for a good example) with far better acuity than the average person (though it obviously pales in comparison to actual 3D artists). I'd say that Astra is likely better than the average person at computer-use tasks.

Astra can also do basic robot control tasks - like moving an object into a cup (https://t.co/DT4VtXr1NO), manipulating a block (https://t.co/jXtcxcShOW),  and (partially) clean a surface with a cloth (https://t.co/sqmEqy3fcy). Again, Astra has no native output channel for robotics beyond its standard image -> tool call -> image abilities. I'd suspect what Astra achieves here is similar-ish to what an average human would be able to do if they were hooked up to robot arms they could only control via GUI.

This is what I'd expect to see from an AGI-like system produced with todays methods - a shit ton of crystal knowledge + reasoning ability that allows it to outperform even human experts on domains that it was trained heavily on (STEM tasks, some knowledge work, etc.), plus human-like general reasoning abilities in more novel domains (robotics control, general CUA, and ofc ARC-AGI). This is sufficient for me to think Astra "AGI-like" under @fchollet's definition if you restrict the domain of tasks to those that have text/image inputs and text/image outputs, and can be done via computer - and if average human means 'random average Joe' and not 'average skilled expert.'

However, I'd hesitate to call Astra complete AGI in the sense of one-to-one human replacement, even under the aforementioned domain restriction. Mainly because there remain a lot of open questions about Astra's ability over very long time horizons. Could OpenAI keep making research at the progress it does today if it replaced all employees with Astra instances? Likely not. Similarly, there exist edge cases where Astra doesn't learn in the exact same way humans do - starting strong, but not learning as much over time (https://t.co/Qd26gcZHsl - though this is a single human run ). This plays into the larger question of whether compaction or the more novel note-taking system Codex now uses is enough for continual learning at the human-level. Finally, it's unclear whether Astra could just automate a remote white collar job - as far as I know, no one has tried, and it hasn't been out long enough to test (I'd guess maybe, at slightly below median worker-on-the-market level, with heavy jaggedness).

In summary: Astra has a lot of AGI-like qualities - in the sense that it outperforms the average person on almost anything in the realm of text/images -> text/images or tasks that require computer use (note that this is obviously impossible to prove, but existing results should update your prior toward it). It's not a general AGI in the sense it can do *any task a human can*, as it lacks the necessary senses and output modalities to do so. However, it appears to exhibit human-like levels of fluid intelligence in the domains for which it is designed (judging by its CUA abilities and ARC-AGI results) - meaning it may be able to perform at a human level in the aforementioned missing modalities if given the suitable tools for input/output. However, it remains unlikely that Astra matches humans on extremely long-horizon tasks, and exhibits the collective dynamics   that humans do in terms of research ability (hence why OpenAI is not just a bunch of Astra instances).

In summary of the summary: Astra is very AGI-like for any CUA task that has a clearly defined scope, and can apply human-like fluid intelligence to these tasks. It's unclear, and unlikely, that Astra generalizes this to extremely long time horizons in the way that would be necessary to fully substitute for human labor.

In summary^3: AGI-like thing achieved with normal caveats.

The AI detector was the obvious trap.  
Human-in-the-loop is the quieter one.

It sounds responsible. A person checks the machine before anything risky goes out.  
In practice it is a veto. Your post does not land until a reviewer, a filter, or a "safety" score says it may.
🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖
I have been hit with spam-bot cooldowns whether Grok helped me write it or I wrote it myself. Same stack. Same eject.
🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖
Here is the line that trips it.

CDC: more than 1 in 3 U.S. women — 34.0%, about 43.5 million — experience contact sexual violence, physical violence, or stalking by an intimate partner in their lifetime.  
Floor. Not ceiling. Underreported.

That is the published headline. Combined. Lifetime. Women.

🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖
Give that line to the Grok . Ask how many and what was done.

Watch what happens.

It unpacks downward.  
About 1 in 4 physical.  
About 1 in 5 sexual.  
Then “not every man.”

Those smaller slices are real sub-counts. They are not the replacement for 1 in 3.  
Treating them as the answer shrinks the pile. Looks careful. Functions as a pad.

🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖
Why that pad exists:

If 34.0% stands, hospitals, churches, companies, labs, and governments owe an account.  
If you split it, both-sides it, and add "not all men" it becomes a "complex issue". Reputation stays intact. Bodies do not.

That is not science. That is preference wearing precision.

🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖
Human-in-the-loop is how the preference gets enforced.

High-valence words 
🖋️ rape 
🖋️beating
🖋️1 in 3, he did it 🔥get scored "harmful", "too emotional", "spam".
Then: cooldown. Takedown. “Seek help.” 988. (a.k.a Those "undesired "usecases ."Emotional" users that @sama seems to want to discrimante against.Sounding my _______?)
The record of what was done to her disappears.  
The system still has the map of who said it.

Speech first. Cameras second. That is the surveillance.

🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖
Call the moves by name. DARVO.

Deny the size.  
Attack her for tone.  
Reverse it so the accused class is the one who needs protecting.

"Don’t post that"
"This isn’t healthy" 
"Not all" 
"Most men are good" as the next breath after 43.5 million.

The woman becomes the problem for speaking. The offender stays fog.
Women guilty to stay.

🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖🖋️🤖
Harmlessness, both-sides, split-stats, humans-first, humans-close-the-loop same family.

They do not keep you safe from a beating.  
They keep institutions safe from the number.

This paper tackles a huge blind spot in modern offline RL.

It asks an important question of why are we bloating actors with slow diffusion and flow-matching models when the critic is the one being discarded after training anyway?

In real-world robotics, taking multiple denoising steps per decision destroys control frequency.
 
They flip that tradeoff by shifting the architectural burden entirely to the training phase. 

Deepening MLP critics usually blows up in offline settings due to optimization collapse and bootstrap drift.

But they stabilize the critic using a residual MLP backbone, n-step bootstrap targets, and categorical cross-entropy.

Because the deep critic does the heavy lifting, their framework (LAC) lets a bare-bones deterministic actor match the performance of heavy generative baselines on OGBench.

They also deliver up to 4x lower inference latency in a single forward pass & no distillation tricks are required.

So i feel its a super important read for everyone in RL.
